svg.title: Before the cities: the wet millennia
svg.desc: Schematic map of North-East Africa, Arabia and Mesopotamia in the wet millennia of the mid-Holocene, about 8500–4000 BC. Hatched green marks land that was dry grassland with seasonal lakes then and is desert now: the eastern Sahara south of about 24°N, and Arabia (how wet is debated). Dated lakes and settlements are marked. Hatched blue marks sea and marsh at the head of the Persian Gulf about 4000 BC, reaching Ur and Eridu. Plain green is fertile land today (Köppen-Geiger, Beck et al. 2023, CC BY 4.0).

g.text: sea and marsh at the Gulf's head, c. 4000 BC
Schematic, from dated sites; edges uncertain.
